modules.name: Path chapters
modules.description: Practical chapters for building and testing an AI app, from first decision to deployment.

tracks.name: Define
tracks.description: Choose the outcome and the people you are building for.

tracks.name: Foundations
tracks.description: Set up Foundry, choose a model, and ground an agent in approved content.

tracks.name: Action Tools
tracks.description: Add tools and require approval before they change anything.

tracks.name: Trust
tracks.description: Test the agent, inspect its traces, and debug failures.

tracks.description: Host the agent and give people a usable way to try it.

outcomes.name: Need an idea first
outcomes.tagline: Find an AI idea small enough to test and useful enough to discuss.
outcomes.description: Use Idea Forge to choose a clear user, a safe sample, and one result you can prove.
success_metrics: A selected idea has an outcome, users, data sources, tier guidance, and risk notes.
The chosen idea maps to relevant lessons, with uncovered work recorded.

outcomes.name: Reference Library
outcomes.tagline: Implementation patterns you can reuse inside a scenario.
outcomes.description: Open an activity when a scenario points you to that capability.
success_metrics: Teams can find the implementation mechanics that support a chosen scenario.
Reference activities stay reusable and do not become a separate customer journey.

scenarios.name: AI Grounding / IQ
scenarios.tagline: Give people useful answers from sources they are allowed to see.
scenarios.customer_outcome: A team can answer one useful set of questions from approved sources, enforce access rules, and show why the answers should be trusted.
decision_prompts: Which user decision or action will trusted context improve?
What access boundary, source owner, and system of record apply?
Should the experience lead with Copilot Studio + SharePoint, Foundry IQ, Fabric IQ, Work IQ, or Web IQ?
What golden dataset and operating evidence will prove the pilot is safe and useful?
Where will users meet the assistant, and who operates it once they do?

lessons.title: Select the source and permission architecture
Build retrieval before adding an agent
Add agent and live-data routing only when justified
Deploy and surface it to users

build_modules.title: Provision Foundry, AI Search, and observability
build_modules.summary: Create the shared keyless foundation and verify its generated environment contract before adding customer data.
build_modules.outcome: Foundations Step 1

build_modules.title: Select the source and permission architecture
build_modules.summary: Choose where approved information lives and which identity is checked when someone asks a question.
build_modules.outcome: Signed source, access, freshness, and system-of-record decision

build_modules.title: Ingest and index approved content
build_modules.summary: Connect the selected source, preserve source/version metadata and access controls, then prove retrieval with a seeded corpus.
build_modules.outcome: Approved documents are discoverable with source metadata

build_modules.title: Compare chat and embedding choices
build_modules.summary: Compare supported deployments on the answer quality the pilot needs, then check latency, cost, and regional capacity.
build_modules.outcome: Foundations Step 2

build_modules.title: Build retrieval before adding an agent
build_modules.summary: Implement citations, abstention, access-denied behavior, and source freshness before deciding whether Foundry IQ or an agent adds value.
build_modules.outcome: Foundations Step 4

build_modules.title: Add agent and live-data routing only when justified
build_modules.summary: Create an agent with explicit source-routing rules and add a verified live-data tool only for a real-time requirement.
build_modules.outcome: Policy and live-data questions route to the correct source

build_modules.title: Evaluate and trace
build_modules.summary: Test citations, access rules, prompt injection, and stale sources. Trace one request from question to answer so you can explain a failure.
build_modules.outcome: Evaluation gate passed with trace and red-team evidence

build_modules.title: Deploy and surface it to users
build_modules.summary: Choose where people will use the agent, pin the version, and verify anonymous, authorized, and restricted calls through that deployed HTTP surface.
build_modules.outcome: Deployed surface passes anonymous, authorized, and restricted HTTP checks

scenarios.name: Content Understanding and Document Workflow
scenarios.tagline: Turn documents into structured results that a person can review.
scenarios.customer_outcome: An expert tests safe document samples, gives engineering a clear JSON contract, and keeps a person in control of the final workflow decision.
decision_prompts: Which document decision creates measurable value when it is faster and more consistent?
Are representative, authorized samples and expected outcomes ready for SME testing?
Where must human review, correction, and evidence be retained in the workflow?
What isolation, access, and promotion controls are required beyond Studio project/analyzer boundaries?

build_modules.title: Provision the shared Foundry foundation
build_modules.summary: Create the keyless Foundry account, chat + embedding deployments, document storage, and observability baseline before adding document services or customer files.
build_modules.outcome: Foundations Step 1

build_modules.title: Connect an approved document source
build_modules.summary: Choose Azure Blob, ADLS Gen2, SharePoint, or OneLake and preserve source identity, version, permissions, and quarantine controls.
build_modules.outcome: Approved intake and document-retention design

build_modules.title: Select the extraction capability
build_modules.summary: Test the available extraction options against real sample quality and the fields reviewers need. Then check region and cost.
build_modules.outcome: Document capability and implementation decision

build_modules.title: Implement typed extraction with evidence
build_modules.summary: Return a validated result with confidence, page references, missing-field handling, and no inferred values.
build_modules.outcome: Structured extraction result and low-confidence failure path

build_modules.title: Build review, correction, and handoff
build_modules.summary: Send uncertain results to a named reviewer. Keep every correction, then pass only approved results to the next system.
build_modules.outcome: Reviewer correction and approval trace

build_modules.title: Evaluate and trace the workflow
build_modules.summary: Measure field accuracy and false approvals across representative documents. Track how often people must review a result and how long the workflow takes.
build_modules.outcome: Scenario evaluation gate and trace review

build_modules.title: Deploy the reviewable workflow
build_modules.summary: Ship the approved workflow behind an authenticated endpoint with managed identity, application monitoring, and a rollback path.
build_modules.outcome: Controlled pilot deployment

scenarios.name: Avatar Scenario
scenarios.tagline: Build an accessible avatar experience that people approve before it goes live.
scenarios.customer_outcome: People get an accessible avatar-led experience, while owners can trace every published claim to its source and the person who approved it.
decision_prompts: Which Azure/Microsoft experience capability (Speech avatar batch, real-time avatar, Voice Live, video translation, or plain audio) fits the pilot's consent, accessibility, latency, language, and cost requirements?
Which communication, learning, or support moment, audience, locale, and channel should the pilot serve first?
Which approved sources and named owners may support the script, and when do they expire?
Who must approve factual accuracy, legal/compliance, brand, and accessibility before anything is published?
How will the experience disclose synthetic/AI assistance, offer human help, and avoid deceptive representation?
Which evaluation, red-team, and operational measures decide whether to iterate, scale, pause, or withdraw?

lessons.title: Module 2 — Provision the Foundry + Speech foundation
Module 3 — Build the governed content pipeline
Module 4 — Build the grounded assistant behind the experience
Module 5 — Generate the accessible avatar experience
Module 6 — Gate publication behind human approval
Module 7 — Evaluate, red-team, trace, and operate

build_modules.title: Verify and select the Azure experience capability
build_modules.summary: Before writing code, confirm which Speech or Voice capability fits the experience. Record its API, region, identity, cost, accessibility limits, consent rules, and release gates.
build_modules.outcome: Dated, evidence-backed capability decision record covering service, API, region, identity, pricing, accessibility, disclosure, and limited-access gating

build_modules.title: Provision the shared Foundry + Speech foundation
build_modules.summary: Deploy the keyless Foundry, model, Azure AI Search, Speech data plane, and observability baseline the avatar experience uses, with managed-identity RBAC and no secrets.
build_modules.outcome: Foundations Steps 1 and 2 plus a keyless .env contract

build_modules.title: Build the governed content pipeline
build_modules.summary: Connect approved content and keep its owner, version, expiry date, and access rules. Use that record to control what the experience may say.
build_modules.outcome: Versioned claim set with authoritative sources, owners, and expiry

build_modules.title: Build the grounded assistant behind the experience
build_modules.summary: Build a model or Foundry agent that drafts from approved content, cites its sources, refuses unsupported claims, and hands uncertain cases to a person.
build_modules.outcome: Foundations Steps 3 and 4 — grounded, citing, refusing agent

build_modules.title: Generate the accessible avatar experience
build_modules.summary: Generate the experience from an approved script revision. Include a synthetic-media notice, captions or a transcript, and a non-avatar fallback.
build_modules.outcome: Accessible experience generated from an approved revision, with disclosure and fallback

build_modules.title: Gate publication behind human approval
build_modules.summary: Version output, collect factual, legal, brand, and accessibility approvals, and implement pause or withdrawal when a source changes.
build_modules.outcome: Approved publication and withdrawal record with a full trace

build_modules.title: Evaluate, red-team, trace, and operate
build_modules.summary: Test whether the experience stays grounded, discloses synthetic media, remains accessible, and hands off correctly. Trace failures before deciding whether to release the pilot.
build_modules.outcome: Pilot scorecard, red-team result, trace review, and release decision
